page: Amazon Web Services c5d.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8124M processor running at 3.4 GHz. The configuration includes 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled as a 100 GB local NVMe SSD instance store, and the baseline network bandwidth is 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the c5d.xlarge exhibits weak to average performance across various workloads. In CPU-focused tests, the instance achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1405.09 and a multi-core score of 3692.85, both falling into the bottom 25%. Geekbench results show an average single-core score of 1142.0 and a weak multi-core score of 2507.0. Memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, with read-only large block bandwidth at 26.2 GB/sec and a PassMark memory score of 1073.65, placing it in the bottom 10%. However, single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression show average performance at 24.03 GB/sec and 9.13 GB/sec respectively.

The primary tradeoff of the c5d.xlarge is its low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:2 and weak multi-threaded scaling, as evidenced by a poor multi-threaded bzip3 decompression score of 16.95 GB/sec. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the inclusion of local NVMe SSD storage provides low-latency scratch space without the added cost of external block storage, though the data is ephemeral. This hardware profile is suited for workloads requiring dedicated CPU allocation and fast local storage but with modest memory demands, such as batch processing, media transcoding, web serving, and distributed analytics.
